rationales: An electron is a particle, not the octet rule.
A picture of electron configuration is not the rule itself.
The rule is not simply a pattern of electronic configuration.
The octet rule describes atoms attaining eight electrons in their valence shell.
Rubber is an amorphous solid.
Plastic is generally an amorphous solid.
Glass is an amorphous solid.
Glucose forms a crystalline solid, so it is not amorphous.
Milk is a colloid and is heterogeneous at the microscopic level.
Ink is generally treated as a uniform mixture in basic classifications, though some inks are colloidal.
Milk of magnesia is a suspension and is heterogeneous.
Sugar dissolves uniformly in water to form a homogeneous mixture.
KCl solubility changes appreciably with temperature.
KNO₃ solubility increases greatly with temperature.
NaNO₃ solubility increases appreciably with temperature.
NaCl solubility changes only slightly with temperature.
Sodium produces a golden-yellow flame.
A brilliant white flame is not the characteristic flame colour of sodium.
Red is not the characteristic flame colour of sodium.
Brick red is characteristic of calcium, not sodium.
Paints are colloidal dispersions, so they are false solutions.
Starch solution is also a colloid, or false solution.
Sugar in water forms a true solution, not a colloid.
Salt in water forms a true solution, not a colloid.
Sugar in water is a solid dissolved in a liquid.
Butter is a colloid with liquid dispersed in a solid medium.
Salt in water is a solid dissolved in a liquid.
Fog is liquid dispersed in a gas.
Sulphur is not reduced when its oxidation state rises from −2 to 0.
H₂S is oxidized as its sulphur changes from oxidation state −2 to 0.
The complete reaction is a redox reaction, but the conversion of H₂S to sulphur is oxidation.
Addition is not the classification of this conversion.
Iron reacts with mineral acids.
Zinc reacts with both acids and alkalis.
Gold is a noble metal and is not affected by mineral acids and alkalis under ordinary conditions.
Sodium reacts vigorously with water and acids.
CO₂ has a molecular mass of 44 amu, not 34 amu.
CO₂ has a molecular mass of 44 amu, not 40 amu.
CO₂ has a molecular mass of 12 + 2(16) = 44 amu.
CO₂ has a molecular mass of 44 amu, not 50 amu.
The O shell has principal quantum number 5 and can have five subshells.
The N shell has principal quantum number 4 and consists of four subshells.
The L shell has principal quantum number 2 and consists of two subshells.
The M shell has principal quantum number 3 and consists of three subshells.
The modern periodic table is not arranged by atomic mass.
The modern periodic table is based on increasing atomic number.
The number of neutrons is not the basis of the modern periodic table.
Atomic radius is not the basis of the modern periodic table.
The configuration ns² does not represent the halogen valence shell.
The configuration ns² np¹ represents Group 13 elements.
The configuration ns² np⁴ represents Group 16 elements.
Halogens have the general valence-shell configuration ns² np⁵.
H₂ has a nonpolar covalent bond because its atoms are identical.
Cl₂ has a nonpolar covalent bond because its atoms are identical.
HCl has a polar covalent bond because chlorine attracts the shared electrons more strongly than hydrogen.
N₂ has a nonpolar covalent bond because its atoms are identical.
The dotted line between water molecules represents a hydrogen bond.
An ionic bond involves attraction between oppositely charged ions, not these water molecules.
A covalent bond joins atoms within a water molecule, not separate water molecules.
A metallic bond occurs between metal atoms, not between water molecules.
